claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially has a high-temperature disordered BCC state.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by a thermodynamic instability.
The thermodynamic instability is driven by high Al chemical activity in the high-temperature disordered BCC state.
Annealing causes Al to segregate to specific lattice sites.
Localized Al enrichment nucleates ordered domains within the BCC matrix.
The ordered domains may exhibit B2 ordering.
Formation of ordered domains shifts phase equilibrium away from the metastable disordered BCC configuration.
Differential diffusion rates permit Al accumulation in regions that nucleate an ordered phase.
Al segregation destabilizes the disordered BCC state through an order-disorder transformation despite kinetic barriers.
Annealed samples will develop XRD superlattice reflections indicative of ordered domains.
Annealed samples will exhibit measurable lattice-parameter shifts.
TEM and EDS will reveal localized regions of increased Al concentration in annealed samples.
Ordering, lattice-parameter changes, and Al enrichment will become more pronounced with increasing annealing time within the applicable temperature window.
Rapid quenching from high temperature retains the disordered BCC phase without significant Al segregation or ordering.
The proposed mechanism operates only at temperatures low enough to provide a thermodynamic driving force for ordering but high enough to provide appreciable atomic mobility.
Ordering will not occur above or below the proposed thermal window.
Controlled isothermal annealing at varied dwell times should be compared with rapid quenching from the high-temperature state.
A lack of superlattice reflections, localized Al enrichment, and ordered domains, together with statistical equivalence to the quenched baseline, would falsify the hypothesis.
